question: Which condition is considered a high-risk factor that rules out a safe home delivery?

options.A: A normal vertex presentation at term
options.B: A history of a previous cesarean section
options.C: A history of a single normal spontaneous vaginal birth
options.D: A maternal age between twenty and thirty

question: Which team member helps a patient regain fine motor skills for daily dressing and eating?

options.A: Physiotherapist
options.B: Occupational therapist
options.C: Medical social worker
options.D: Speech-language pathologist

explanation: Occupational therapists (OTs) focus on everyday activities and hand coordination, while physiotherapists focus more on walking and big movements. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is a cystocele?

options.A: Benign smooth muscle tumors growing inside the myometrium
options.B: Bulging of the bladder into the anterior vaginal wall
options.C: Herniation of the rectum into the posterior vaginal canal
options.D: Downward displacement of the uterus through the cervix

explanation: A cystocele happens when the supportive tissue between a woman's bladder and vaginal wall weakens, allowing the bladder to sag into the vagina. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why must a tiny opening be deliberately left when performing infibulation?

options.A: To ensure future surgical procedures are easier to perform
options.B: To allow the passage of urine and menstrual blood
options.C: To allow air circulation inside the reproductive tract
options.D: To prevent complete closure of the abdominal cavity

explanation: Even with infibulation, a small opening is necessary so that essential body fluids like urine and menses can still leave the body. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T3#GNS312_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is a 'just culture' so important in a healthcare facility?

options.A: It forces every nurse to work double shifts without taking breaks

options.C: It guarantees that doctors receive higher salaries than nurses
options.D: It encourages staff to report errors and near-misses without fear

question: What happens inside the body to cause muscle wasting (atrophy) during long periods of bed rest?

options.A: Rapid increase in slow-twitch muscle fibers
options.B: Excessive production of new muscle fibers
options.C: Protein breakdown happens faster than protein building
options.D: Permanent hardening of the bone marrow

question: A client requests an IUD right after receiving treatment for an incomplete abortion. What is the best clinical action?

options.C: Refuse the request and insist she returns after three normal menstrual cycles
options.D: Provide the IUD immediately on the same day if no severe infection is present

question: Why did ancient medical practices often combine spiritual rituals with herbal remedies?

options.A: Healers had no way to treat patients without praying first.
options.B: Spiritual chants increased the chemical potency of plant extracts.
options.C: Early laws strictly required religious approval before giving medicine.
options.D: Illness was frequently believed to be caused by supernatural forces.

question: A community nurse meets resistance from male elders who think family planning promotes promiscuity. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the elders completely and hand out contraceptives secretly behind their backs

options.C: Argue with them aggressively to prove that their traditional beliefs are entirely wrong
options.D: Report the entire village community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Community health nursing requires patience and respect. Sitting down to talk with community leaders helps frame family planning around health, peace, and family well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h6)

question: A spouse is blocked from working and denied access to family money. What type of abuse is this?

options.A: Economic abuse
options.B: Psychological abuse
options.C: Traditional maltreatment
options.D: Physical violence

explanation: Exactly! Controlling someone's finances makes them financially dependent, which is a key tactic abusers use to trap victims. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h2)

question: What are the two most common major causes of antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Ectopic pregnancy and bloody show
options.B: Placenta praevia and abruptio placentae
options.C: Uterine rupture and cervical polyps
options.D: Vasa praevia and gestational diabetes

explanation: Placenta praevia and abruptio placentae are responsible for the vast majority of heavy bleeding episodes in the late stages of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h2)

question: Why must nurses wear gloves or use a tool when applying certain topical medications?

options.A: To keep the patient's room completely sterile
options.B: To prevent absorbing the medication through their own skin
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling cold during touch
options.D: To ensure the medication absorbs faster into the patient

explanation: Powerful drugs like hormone creams can soak right through your bare hands if you aren't wearing gloves. Always protect yourself too! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is another common term used to describe a brand name drug?

options.A: Generic identifier
options.B: Chemical name
options.C: Universal formula
options.D: Proprietary name

explanation: A brand name is also called a proprietary name because the company 'properly' owns the rights to that specific marketing title. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h3)

question: What happens to the mother's heart output right after the placenta is delivered?

options.B: It experiences an initial rapid increase due to autotransfusion
options.C: It remains completely steady for exactly six weeks
options.D: It reverses direction and flows backward into the veins

question: Why is a democratic leadership style poorly suited for a sudden emergency in the emergency department?

options.A: Gathering opinions takes too much time
options.B: It leads to too many medical errors
options.C: Staff members usually refuse to speak
options.D: Doctors are not allowed to participate

explanation: Democratic processes require time for discussion, which is dangerous when immediate life-saving action is needed. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which nursing action helps most with the social and emotional challenges of chronic epilepsy?

options.A: Focusing solely on medication dosages and ignoring emotional health
options.B: Isolating the patient from family to reduce external stress
options.C: Encouraging the patient to hide their diagnosis from employers
options.D: Providing counseling resources and addressing social stigma

explanation: Epilepsy carries a lot of societal stigma in many communities. Offering support, education, and counseling helps patients build confidence and live full lives. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h8)

question: Why is it important to interview a patient suspected of experiencing GBV alone, without family members present?

options.A: To comply with visiting hour restrictions set by hospital management
options.B: To prevent family members from asking questions about medical costs
options.C: To ensure the patient feels safe to speak honestly without fear of retaliation
options.D: To save time during busy hospital shift change periods

explanation: Abusive partners or controlling family members may intimidate the patient, preventing them from disclosing the truth if they remain in the room. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h7)

question: When do expectant mothers usually notice that their vulval varicose veins hurt or ache the most?

options.A: Directly after a heavy meal
options.B: Immediately upon waking up in the morning
options.C: After standing or walking for a long time
options.D: While resting flat on their back

explanation: Gravity is the culprit here! Staying on your feet all day lets blood pool downward, so by evening, the pressure and ache feel much stronger. Rest and elevation are best friends here. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h3)

question: The sagittal suture connects which two bones of the foetal skull?

options.A: The frontal and parietal bones
options.B: The two parietal bones
options.C: The temporal and frontal bones
options.D: The parietal and occipital bones

explanation: Think of the sagittal suture as the line running right down the middle of the top of the head, joining the left and right parietal bones together! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h2)

question: Why should you keep a client's neck straight and in a neutral position when managing high ICP?

options.A: Straight necks make it easier for the client to chew their meals
options.B: It keeps the breathing tube securely taped to the side of the mouth
options.C: It prevents the client from accidentally pulling out their intravenous lines
options.D: Bending the neck can kink jugular veins and trap blood in the head

explanation: Great to know for clinicals! Twisting or bending the neck blocks blood from draining out of the brain, causing it to back up and shoot up the intracranial pressure. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h4)

question: What is a cardiovascular complication?

options.A: A side effect caused by taking too many vitamins
options.B: A normal reaction to doing heavy exercise
options.C: A brand new primary heart disease
options.D: A secondary problem that happens after initial heart or blood vessel damage

explanation: Think of a complication as a follow-up problem. When the heart or blood vessels are already damaged, other issues pop up because the body's normal coping systems get overwhelmed. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which symptom is a classic peripheral adverse effect of anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Watery diarrhea
options.B: Dry mouth
options.C: Narrowed pupils
options.D: Excessive drooling

explanation: Blocking parasympathetic activity decreases saliva production, leading to noticeable dry mouth. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h5)

question: Which tool is best for collecting a clean soil sample for microbial isolation?

options.A: A bare human hand pressed directly onto top dirt
options.B: An unsterilized wooden stick from the ground
options.C: A sterile trowel from a few centimeters below the surface
options.D: A household sponge soaked in soapy water

explanation: Well done! Digging slightly under the topsoil with a sterile tool helps you avoid dried-out dirt and outside germs. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h3)

question: Who on the healthcare team mainly helps patients with swallowing problems?

options.A: Speech-Language Pathologist
options.B: Occupational Therapist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Physical Therapist

explanation: Spot on! Speech therapists don't just help with talking—they are experts at checking if swallowing is safe, too. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h2)

question: What is the danger of giving a central cough suppressant to a patient who has a chest full of thick mucus?

options.A: The mucus instantly dissolves into clear water.
options.B: Blood pressure drops to dangerous levels.
options.C: Mucus can accumulate and block the airways.
options.D: The patient begins breathing twice as fast.

question: Why is knowing the location of the dorsal penile nerves important during a circumcision?

options.A: It controls the blood flow to the entire lower abdomen

options.C: It helps prevent accidental removal of the urethral opening
options.D: It ensures the scrotal skin heals without any scarring

question: Which disease is classically transmitted via the airborne route?

options.A: Scabies

options.C: Malaria
options.D: Tuberculosis

question: Why is cardiac syncope considered the most dangerous type of fainting?

options.A: It is almost impossible to diagnose with standard hospital equipment.
options.B: It causes permanent brain damage within just a few seconds.
options.C: It is frequently linked to serious heart rhythm problems or structural disease.
options.D: It only happens when the patient is actively exercising or working.

explanation: Cardiac syncope stems from heart issues that carry a high risk of sudden cardiac arrest if left untreated. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which substance builds up in the joints to trigger a painful gout attack?

options.A: Infected purulent white blood cells
options.B: Monosodium urate crystals
options.C: Excess synovial lubricating fluid
options.D: Calcium pyrophosphate deposits

question: What are the two main types of artificial replacement valves used in heart surgery?

options.A: Mechanical and bioprosthetic
options.B: Autologous skin and muscle
options.C: Silicone and nylon mesh
options.D: Plastic and synthetic rubber

explanation: Replacement valves are either mechanical (made of tough man-made materials) or bioprosthetic (crafted from animal tissue, like pig or cow tissue). [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h9)

question: Which of these strategies directly helps nurses avoid burnout by giving them more control over their time?

options.A: Mandatory double shifts on weekends
options.B: Flexible scheduling options
options.C: Eliminating all scheduled meal breaks
options.D: Strictly fixed vacation blackouts

explanation: Giving nurses a say in their shifts helps them balance family, rest, and school—a huge shield against burnout! [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h5)

question: What does the term 'bereavement' mean in nursing care?

options.A: The physical pain felt in the chest after a loss

question: A patient is being discharged after treatment for pelvic inflammatory disease. What key advice should you give her?

options.C: Avoid drinking water for two days.

question: Which outside group is most important for a school to partner with when planning student immunizations?

options.A: International tourism boards

question: Why is fluoroscopy a key component of a barium swallow test?

options.A: It provides real-time moving images of swallowing and peristalsis

options.C: It measures the exact pH levels inside the stomach

explanation: Unlike standard still X-rays, fluoroscopy acts like an X-ray movie, letting the radiologist watch how food and liquid move down the throat in real time. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h1)

question: What practice helps germs develop resistance to chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Allowing alcohol-based hand rubs to air-dry completely on the skin
options.B: Changing cleaning cloths and disinfecting solutions after every single room
options.C: Washing hands with soap and water after caring for every infectious patient
options.D: Using disinfectants at too weak a dilution or cutting down the required contact time

question: A teenage girl visits the clinic with recurrent chest infections and unusual linear burns across her breasts. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Breast ironing abuse

question: Which sign might mean a patient's bowel was accidentally injured during laparoscopy?

options.A: Mild itching around the small skin puncture sites

options.D: Temporary hoarseness of the patient's voice

question: Someone is caught helping a traditional cutter prepare instruments for FGM. Under the VAPP Act, what is this helper's legal status?

question: What happens when a sterile item touches a non-sterile surface?

question: Where should a patient place their body weight when walking with crutches?

question: What is the main goal of sterilization?

question: In a community health project, money, medical supplies, and trained personnel are known as what?

options.A: Inputs

question: What makes environmental reservoirs different from human and animal reservoirs?

question: What is the main job of a receptor in a reflex pathway?

question: A patient with severe diarrhoea complains of dizziness when standing up quickly. What does this finding suggest?

question: What does patient acuity measure in workforce planning?

options.B: How long a patient stays admitted on the ward

question: Why does a nurse need to ask when a patient's symptoms first started?

options.C: Insurance companies require exact dates before approving lab tests

question: How do common hormonal contraceptives (like pills and injectables) mainly prevent pregnancy?

question: What level of cleaning is needed for items that only touch intact, healthy skin?

question: Why should a nurse avoid using household kitchen spoons to measure liquid medications?

options.A: Using them makes the liquid spill on the table
options.B: Household spoons react chemically with liquid drugs
options.C: Kitchen spoons are too heavy for patients to hold
options.D: Kitchen spoons vary in size and give inaccurate doses

question: A pregnant patient with hyperemesis has low potassium and high blood pH. What is happening?

options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

question: How do clinical audits and incident reports help nursing management?

options.C: By automatically transferring legal liability to the hospital board
options.D: By providing control mechanisms to monitor performance and correct standard deviations

explanation: Audits and incident reports act as safety nets. They help managers spot mistakes early, track quality, and keep patient care standards high. [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why would you choose a subcutaneous injection instead of an IV for certain drugs like insulin?

options.C: To prevent any local skin irritation

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient taking oral prednisone to protect their stomach?

question: What is the primary rule when examining a limb for musculoskeletal problems?

options.C: Always start by performing an X-ray before touching the limb
options.D: Always compare the affected side with the unaffected side

question: What is the best eating strategy for a patient dealing with severe nausea and poor appetite?

options.C: Withholding all food until appetite returns spontaneously

question: Which parts of the body usually show the earliest physical signs of a nutrient deficiency?

question: What is the main goal of secondary stroke prevention strategies?

options.C: To reverse existing brain cell death and restore lost tissue
options.D: To cure the underlying genetic cause of high blood pressure

question: Where are the free nerve endings that pick up pain mostly found?

question: How does constant stress on a very busy hospital ward affect a nurse's day-to-day interactions?

question: Which device delivers a shock to stop dangerous, irregular heart rhythms?

question: Why should you check physical vital signs alongside what a patient tells you?

question: When is the best time to document a rectal suppository in the patient's records?

question: What is a major focus of infection control education during community health nursing outreach?

question: Why is a CT scan usually the go-to emergency test for sudden head injuries?

question: Why is continuous heart monitoring a must right after a successful defibrillation?

question: A patient who just had cataract surgery asks why they must avoid heavy lifting. What is the best nursing response?

question: What is the main goal of a cerebral angiography test?

question: What causes the blood vessels in a newborn's lungs to relax and open up at birth?

question: How should a nurse touch a newly applied plaster cast while it is still wet?

question: What is one of the main ways community health nurses use incidence data?

question: Your patient just had surgery and has painful trapped gas. What is the best first nursing action?

question: Which of these findings is completely normal and NOT a sign of heart stress?

question: What is the main role of multimodal sensory association areas?

question: A patient with severe pre-eclampsia is being transferred from a primary health center to a teaching hospital. What must the midwife send along?

question: A staff nurse wants to learn advanced wound care techniques and earn a promotion to ward sister. What do these desires represent?

question: What is the main job of haustrations (pocket-like folds) in the colon?

question: Which lifestyle habit is a known trigger that worsens inflammation in rheumatic conditions?

question: Why must patients finish their full course of TB drugs even after they start feeling better?

question: A nurse is teaching an antenatal class about preventing back strain. Which advice is best to share?

options.B: Wound looks much better today and the client is very happy with it
options.C: Wound is healing nicely as expected without any nurse assistance
options.D: Wound bed pink, 2cm by 3cm, covered with dry sterile gauze; no foul odor

explanation: Objective documentation uses measurable sizes, colors, and specific descriptions rather than vague subjective opinions like 'looks much better.' [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h5)

question: What should a nurse do if a sterile instrument pack has a torn or damp wrapper?

options.A: Discard or return the item because sterility is lost
options.B: Wipe the outside with alcohol and place it back on the shelf
options.C: Use it quickly before any dust can settle inside
options.D: Ask another nurse to approve using it for a minor dressing

explanation: Any damage or moisture to a sterile wrapper compromises the barrier, meaning the instruments are no longer safe to use. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: Why do you hold the first removed glove inside the palm of your remaining gloved hand?

options.A: To stop the latex from releasing powder into the air
options.B: To easily peel off the second glove without touching its dirty outside
options.C: To keep the first glove clean so you can use it again
options.D: To save space in the waste bin

explanation: Ball up the first glove in your palm so your bare fingers can safely slide under the clean inner cuff of the second glove. Clever and safe! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the main reason a nursing student is in the operating theatre?

options.A: To administer anaesthetic medications independently
options.B: To replace the scrub nurse during complex procedures
options.C: To act as the primary circulating nurse for major cases
options.D: To learn and observe surgical nursing care firsthand

explanation: As a student, you are there to gain experience, connect your classroom notes to real-life practice, and learn safely under supervision! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h7)

question: Which of these does NOT normally change the incidence of a disease in a population?

options.A: The introduction of better diagnostic testing tools
options.B: The total number of historical hospital building designs
options.C: Environmental changes affecting vector breeding
options.D: Mass immunization and vaccination campaigns

explanation: Correct! Hospital architecture won't directly stop or spread infections the way vaccines or environmental changes do. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h5)

question: Before opening a standard catheter kit, which major allergies must you always check for?

options.A: Penicillin and sulfa
options.B: Latex and iodine
options.C: Insulin and heparin
options.D: Paracetamol and aspirin

explanation: Always double-check! Standard kits usually contain latex tubing and iodine cleansers, so catching an allergy early saves your patient a lot of pain. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h4)

question: What exactly is a 'prodrug'?

options.A: A vitamin supplement taken before meals to enhance drug absorption
options.B: A chemical that completely blocks liver enzymes from working
options.C: An old medication that has been replaced by newer pharmaceutical formulations
options.D: A medication administered in an inactive form that relies on metabolism to become active

explanation: A prodrug is like a secret agent! It is given in an inactive form and relies on your body's metabolic processes to switch it 'on' so it can do its therapeutic job. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a performance appraisal in nursing management?

options.A: To find reasons to terminate employee contracts immediately
options.B: To replace daily clinical supervision entirely
options.C: To evaluate job performance and guide professional growth
options.D: To decide which nurse gets the biggest office space

explanation: Appraisals measure work against standards to help staff improve their clinical practice and develop professionally. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h6)

question: A patient with active TB is on the ward. Which nursing action directly targets the human reservoir?

options.A: Checking the ward's water supply for bacterial contamination
options.B: Teaching the family about proper kitchen ventilation
options.C: Providing emotional counselling on chronic illness
options.D: Administering the prescribed anti-tuberculosis medications

explanation: Giving the right medications kills the germs inside the patient's body, wiping out the human reservoir directly. Great clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Providing emergency surgery for severe trauma victims
options.B: Managing end-stage organ failure with palliative care
options.C: Early detection and prompt intervention for mild problems
options.D: Preventing a disease from ever occurring in a healthy person

explanation: Secondary prevention catches conditions early when they are easiest to treat and manage successfully. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h7)

question: How does low educational level directly affect a family's health?

options.A: It causes physical body changes that bring infections
options.B: It limits job choices and makes it harder to understand health advice
options.C: It stops adults from ever stepping into a pharmacy
options.D: It automatically makes all children drop out of school

explanation: Well done! When reading and schooling are limited, finding steady income is tougher, and grasping medication timetables or health tips becomes a real challenge. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h2)

question: What is the best way to check if a patient actually knows how to use a new inhaler after counselling?

options.A: Checking their vital signs twice a day
options.B: Asking the ward supervisor for approval
options.C: Asking the patient to demonstrate how they use it
options.D: Reading the manufacturer instructional manual

explanation: Watching the patient perform the physical technique is the only true way to know if they can apply your instructions correctly. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h8)

question: In community health, why do leaders rely more on personal trust than strict job titles?

options.A: Formal authority only works inside large urban teaching hospitals
options.B: Community members do not respect official government titles
options.C: Volunteers and local leaders answer to community norms, not job descriptions
options.D: Health nurses are not allowed to give direct orders in villages

explanation: Since most people helping out in the community aren't clocking in as direct employees, building genuine trust and good relationships is key to getting things done. Great job thinking this through! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h1)

question: What does client-centered care focus on the most when dealing with reproductive health?

options.A: The traditional beliefs of the senior medical doctors
options.B: The rigid scheduling needs of the hospital administration
options.C: The personal preferences and autonomy of the individual
options.D: The financial targets set by the facility management

explanation: Brilliant! Client-centered care puts the patient in the driver's seat, respecting their personal choices and rights over their own body. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h3)
